cells.nuance: Monks and nuns under acharyas; the laity is organized around their example and instruction.

cells.label: Non-missionary
cells.nuance: Open in principle, a birth community in practice.

cells.label: Eternal, no creator
cells.nuance: The universe is uncreated and everlasting, moving through cosmic half-cycles.
Digambara monks renounce clothing, Svetambara wear white; some orders veil the mouth; lay dress follows custom.
Nonviolence extended to all beings, joined to truthfulness and non-possession.

cells.label: Ascetic self-purification
cells.nuance: Liberation comes by halting and shedding karma through nonviolence, truthfulness, and austerity.

cells.label: Agamas, disputed canon
cells.nuance: Position 1: Svetambara tradition holds the surviving Agamas to be the authentic canon. Position 2: Digambara tradition holds the original canon lost and relies on later digests. Both revere the Tattvartha Sutra.
cells.contested_note: Position 1: Svetambara tradition holds the surviving Agamas to be the authentic canon. Position 2: Digambara tradition holds the original canon lost and relies on later digests. Both revere the Tattvartha Sutra.

cells.label: Many-sidedness
cells.nuance: Anekantavada treats rival views as partial perspectives rather than plain falsehoods.
Image worship or aniconic assembly by order, with confession and fasting cycles.
